links.outcome: Local retrospective diagnostic performance of AI LVO detection versus neuroradiologist reference standard
links.effect: Sensitivity 84%, specificity 95%, accuracy 93% among 531 CTA examinations; sensitivity 94% for ICA/proximal M1, 87% intermediate, 73% distal M1.
links.quote: Overall LVO detection showed a sensitivity of 84%, specificity of 95%, and accuracy of 93%.

links.outcome: AI sensitivity for occlusions by location, supporting adjunct rather than standalone use
links.effect: Lower sensitivity for distal M1 (73%, κ = 0.48) and nontarget occlusions excluded; authors conclude e-CTA should be adjunctive, not standalone.
links.quote: However, lower sensitivity for intermediate and distal M1 occlusions and the exclusion of nontarget occlusions from the primary endpoint indicate that e-CTA should be used as an adjunctive workflow tool rather than as a standalone method for treatment decision-making.

links.outcome: Time to diagnostic conclusion with versus without AI assistance across reader experience levels
links.effect: AI assistance significantly reduced time to diagnostic conclusion across all reader profiles.
links.quote: AI assistance significantly reduced time to diagnostic conclusion across all reader profiles.

screen.reason: The study evaluates a commercial stroke imaging AI tool (Brainomix e-CTA) in a retrospective cohort, measuring diagnostic performance across occlusion types and comparing readers' time to diagnostic conclusion with versus without AI assistance.

primary.practice: AI assistance vs unassisted reader interpretation
